Alex / team — adding technical sizing notes and commercial framing below. Short answers first, details after.

Short answers (high-level):
- Throughput guidance (typical, multi-tenant real workloads):
  - A100 (80GB) serving quantized Llama/GPT-like weights, 8k context: ~18k–28k tokens/sec per GPU observed (depends on batch and prompt length).
  - H100 (80GB) for 8k context: ~32k–48k tokens/sec per GPU; for 32k context, expect a ~2–2.5x reduction in tokens/sec due to KV cache pressure and attention memory.
- Slotting/backfill policy:
  - Reserved pool = pinned capacity for your tenant; soft-burst lanes configured for short-term overage (usually up to 20–30% of reserved pool)
  - When saturated, priority lanes are: SLA-critical routes -> pinned models -> best-effort/backfill. Backfill jobs are preemptible and eligible for graceful eviction with a 10s token-stop window (configurable).
- Expected RTO for backfill collisions: 1–3 minutes for automated fallback to a compatible quantized variant; 10–15 minutes for capacity re-shuffle where additional GPUs must be reprovisioned.

Sizing & commercial recommendations:
- If you have steady 1B tokens/day at p95 latency budgets, a conservative starting commit is: 8x H100 equivalent (for mixed production + canaries), with a 12–16% burst buffer.
- Commit tiers: 3/6/12 month with discounted burst uplift; longer commits reduce per-token uplift and give higher priority for backfill slots during constrained windows.

Detailed notes: (numbers are examples to be validated in workshop)
- A100 (80GB) guidance: throughput highly sensitive to sequence length and whether models are quantized to 4-bit. With 4-bit quantization and kernel fusion we see the higher end of the range above.
- H100 guidance: best for 32k-context or large batch workloads; gives double-digit improvement for large decoder-only models when KV cache fits.
- Backfill mechanics: we maintain a backfill queue with preemption tokens. Backfill tasks get a low-priority token allowance; they are checkpointed every N tokens for graceful resume.

I'll include a small worked example in the worksheet — mapping your sample traffic to A100/H100 equivalents and recommended commit.

Alex — attaching the excerpted runbook here in-line so procurement/ops can see the operational commitments. This is intentionally prescriptive.

----- BEGIN RUNBOOK EXCERPT -----
Alerting thresholds (example):
- Reserved pool utilization > 85% for 5m -> Alert "RESERVED_POOL_HIGH_UTIL" (severity P2)
- Burst lane utilization > 95% for 2m -> Alert "BURST_EXHAUSTED" (severity P1)
- Preemptions/sec > 5 in 1m -> Alert "BACKFILL_PREEMPTION_SPIKE" (severity P1)

Automated remediation steps (order):
1) Route low-priority traffic to best-effort pool (automated, <30s).
2) Fallback to quantized model variant (automated, <60s) if available and quality thresholds met.
3) If still saturated, promote configured burst capacity (customer-configured burst window).
4) If saturation persists >15m, page on-call SRE and initiate slotting re-balance (manual, expected RTO 10–15m).

Operational notes:
- Preemption grace period: default 10s token-stream flush + checkpoint. Can be increased to 30s for streaming-critical workloads at the expense of reduced backfill throughput.
- Monitoring: We expose token/sec, active_slots, preemptions, avg_latency_p95 per route; suggested dashboards and two example alert queries are included in the attachment.

Example escalation text for customers: "We're currently at 97% of reserved capacity and have initiated burst lanes. We're promoting quantized variants for best-effort routes; SRE is standing by if condition persists."

----- END RUNBOOK EXCERPT -----

Let us know if you want us to convert this to your incident template.

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Console

Commercial summary (initial):
- 6-month commit: 10% discount on baseline per-token, burst uplift +22% during configured windows, standard backfill priority (best-effort preemptible).
- 12-month commit: 16% discount baseline, burst uplift +15%, higher priority for backfill slots (reduces preemption probability by ~35% in constrained windows).
